feedback: Staff at the cafeteria counter are always polite and quick with orders.
The lab computers show a software update reminder pop-up every day, which is slightly annoying.
The university shuttle service was canceled without notice, leaving hundreds of students stranded with no way to get to campus.
Restroom floors are often wet and slippery, could be a safety hazard.
The campus Wi-Fi network was renamed this month, and the connection speed seems about the same as before.
A coffee cart now opens in the student lounge from 7 am to 10 am on weekdays.
The new projector gives a bright picture, but the remote control is missing and the HDMI cable keeps failing.
The cafeteria will be closed for two hours on Friday for a scheduled facility inspection.
Several students got stomach aches and food poisoning after eating the chicken meal at the cafeteria.
The lost and found box is always locked and nobody knows who has the key.
Several power outlets near the reading tables are broken and haven't been fixed in weeks.
I really appreciate how quiet and well-organized the library has become this semester.
The elevator in the main building has been out of service for weeks, so students with disabilities cannot reach the upper floors.
The programming lectures are interesting, but there are not enough lab sessions to practice what we learn.
The lounge Wi-Fi is fast in the morning, but it becomes very slow and keeps dropping after lunch.
Book collection in the CS section is outdated, most titles are from over ten years ago.
The updated coding software installed in the lab is faster and easier to use than the old version.
The lounge tables are wobbly and there are not enough chairs for the number of students.
One of the phone charging ports in the lounge is loose, though the other ports work fine.
Some reference books for my subject are not up to date, but I can find alternatives online.
The cafeteria is a bit warm around noon, though the fans help a little.
Staff at the library help desk were very friendly and helped me find resources quickly.
The renovated restrooms in the new wing are clean, modern, and well-stocked.
Cafeteria tables and trays are often left dirty, and the floor is greasy after lunch.
The emergency exit in the library is partly blocked by stacked boxes.
Electrical outlets near the front of the room don't work, we can't charge our laptops.
Guards at the entrance are courteous and help visitors find their way.
The new shuttle route from the parking area to the main building saves a lot of walking time.
New mesh Wi-Fi system installed this semester covers the whole campus well.
There are exposed electrical wires hanging near the computers in Lab 2, which could give someone an electric shock.
Air conditioning in the library is too weak during afternoon hours, it gets uncomfortably warm.
The library internet is very slow in the afternoons, pages take a full minute to load.
New signage at the campus entrance makes navigation much clearer for visitors.
Loud construction noise next to the lounge makes it impossible to study or rest.
Our exam schedule was changed without notice and several exams now overlap, so many students may miss one of them.
The student organization fair was a fun event and I met many new friends.
Cafeteria ran out of food options by 1pm, students who arrive later have no choices left.
Several monitors in Lab 3 have dead pixels and flickering screens that strain the eyes.
The library catalog search website often shows errors and does not find books that are on the shelves.
Restroom ventilation is poor, there's a persistent unpleasant smell most days.
There are a few candy wrappers scattered near the guard house, but nothing serious.
The cafeteria has tasty food and friendly cooks, but the queue is very slow and they often run out of drinks.
The library roof leaks badly during rain, and water drips over the computers and the bookshelves.
The renovated classroom with new desks is much more comfortable than before.
The lounge is a comfortable place to relax between classes, well maintained overall.
Campus Wi-Fi disconnects constantly in the engineering building, very frustrating.
IT support responded quickly when I reported the Wi-Fi outage near the cafeteria.
New lab computers installed this semester are fast and run our software smoothly.
Vending machines in the student lounge are frequently out of stock or broken.
The jeepney drop-off point was moved to the left side of the gate this week.
Security guards check bags politely and I feel safe entering the campus every day.
Software licenses expired on several machines, we can't run our development tools anymore.
Wi-Fi went down across the whole engineering building during the online midterm exam, and many students lost their answers.
Projector in Room 204 keeps flickering and shutting off in the middle of lectures.
The library replaced its old photocopiers with new machines that work fast and print clearly.
The professor gives very heavy assignments with unclear instructions, and it is hard to catch up.
The new vegetarian options at the cafeteria are delicious and reasonably priced.
Sidewalk near the campus entrance is cracked and uneven, a tripping hazard.
There is no shade or waiting area near the entrance during hot weather.
The Wi-Fi signal in the far corner of the cafeteria is a bit weak, but it is only a minor inconvenience.
The new rice bowl meals at the cafeteria are delicious, cheap and served hot.
Wi-Fi speed near the library is fast and reliable, great for downloading resources.
The library Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting every few minutes, making it hard to research.
The online learning platform is easy to navigate, but it logs us out every ten minutes during quizzes.
The shuttle is a big help on rainy days, but it only runs twice in the morning and is always full.
Drainage in the parking lot is poor, it floods heavily after any rain.
Seating space in the cafeteria is not enough during peak hours, many students eat standing.
The newly renovated library study cubicles are spacious, bright and very comfortable.
The library website now has an updated login page, and the features look the same as before.
The new self-checkout kiosk for borrowing books is fast and very convenient.
Security guards at the parking entrance are attentive and check IDs properly.
The lab technician replaced our mouse and keyboard right away when I reported the issue.
The IT department upgraded the Wi-Fi routers and the connection is much more stable now.
The bulletin board near the entrance shows announcements for upcoming student events.
The exam software in the lab crashed halfway through the test and all our unsaved answers were lost.
The classroom chairs are broken and uncomfortable, some have loose screws.
Trash isn't collected often enough in the lounge, bins overflow by midday.
The air conditioning unit makes a loud rattling noise that distracts during lectures.
The cafeteria added self-service water stations which is a nice convenient touch.
The microphone in the lecture room is broken, so students at the back cannot hear the teacher.
The restroom floor near the gym is flooded and slippery, and a student already fell and got injured.
Air conditioning in the computer lab is excellent, keeps the equipment and students cool.
The hooks on the restroom stall doors are missing, which is a small inconvenience.
The tutoring sessions organized at the library have helped me understand calculus much better.
The entrance was recently repainted and looks much more welcoming now.
There are not enough parking slots for motorcycles, and many students circle for 20 minutes to find a spot.
A fire drill will be held on Thursday at 10 am, and all classes are expected to join.
Lines at the cafeteria during lunch hour are extremely long, sometimes over 30 minutes.
The restroom near the gym is filthy, with overflowing toilets and a sewage smell that makes it unusable and unhealthy.
It takes more than two weeks to get a replacement student ID and the office staff are not helpful.
The cafeteria food is often served cold and the portions are very small for the price.
A loose floor tile in the lounge could make someone trip, but so far nobody has been hurt.
The library has placed recycling bins for paper beside the main door.
Too many students on the same Wi-Fi network causes it to slow down significantly.
Connection near the gymnasium is nonexistent, we can't access online resources there.
The lab received a batch of new keyboards this week, and they are the same model as the old ones.
The restrooms are cleaned regularly in the morning, but they are dirty and smelly again by the afternoon.
The snack stall near the entrance sometimes has no change for large bills, a small annoyance.
The new trees and garden near the campus entrance make the area cool, green and pleasant.
The lab is well-maintained and the seats are comfortable for long programming sessions.
There aren't enough charging stations for laptops in the library, especially near exam week.
The bulletin board near the library has expired posters that nobody removes.
Lighting in the classroom is dim, making it hard to read slides from the back row.
The library is spotless every morning, the cleaning staff do a great job.
Janitors clean the student lounge every day at 5 pm after classes end.
The trees around the parking area give nice shade, but the lot floods with muddy water every time it rains.
New parking lines and signage make it much easier to find a spot now.
The redesigned student lounge with bean bags and plants feels very inviting.
Internet speed in the computer lab is now excellent, large downloads finish in seconds.
Parking area is full by 8am, students have to park far off campus and walk in.
Internet connection in the computer lab drops constantly, especially during peak hours.
Wi-Fi in the dormitory areas is unreliable especially in the evening.
The heat inside the classrooms reaches dangerous levels in the afternoon, and several students have felt dizzy and fainted.
The student council events are fun, but the announcements are always posted at the last minute.
Acoustics in the lecture hall are poor, it's hard to hear the professor from the back.
Midterm exams will be held next week, and the schedule is posted on the bulletin board.
Traffic flow at the entrance is chaotic, tricycles and cars block each other constantly.
Wi-Fi signal in the student lounge is weak compared to other parts of campus.
Lighting in the parking area at night is very dim, feels unsafe walking to the car.
Wi-Fi coverage doesn't reach the outdoor benches near the quadrangle at all.
Restroom on the third floor has a broken faucet that has been leaking for days.
New whiteboards installed in the building are a huge improvement for lectures.
The new CCTV cameras make the parking area feel safer, but the lot is still very dark at night and some lamps are out.
Several lab computers will not turn on at all, so half of the class could not take the practical exam.
The new lecture hall seats are comfortable, but there are far too few power sockets and the door lock is broken.
The bike rack in the parking area is a bit far from the buildings, but it is usable.
The student lounge sofas are torn and worn out, they need replacement.
Classroom is too small for the number of students enrolled, we barely have space.
